articles.title: The fastest double-to-string algorithm you’ve never heard of
articles.summary: The binary-to-decimal conversion library yy from ibireme uses a double-to-string algorithm to find the shortest decimal $\sigma \cdot 10^{e_{10}}$ that round-trips back to a binary float $v$ by intersecting $v$'s rounding interval with decimal grids of various spacings. This is achieved through a fixed-point approximation of $\log_{10} 2$, precomputed power-of-10 tables, and the use of only one multiplication by a precomputed power of 10 in fixed-width integer arithmetic. The library's performance is comparable to that of classic Schubfach, but with a significant reduction in computational overhead.

articles.title: Performance impact of Alignment
articles.summary: Alignment of memory accesses in SIMD vectorization has a significant impact on performance. This includes alignment of loads and stores, which affects auto-vectorization and explicit vectorization. Alignment size is typically 64 bytes for vectors, but can vary depending on the element size and array structure. Unaligned access can lead to errors or incorrect execution, while aligned access is generally faster due to reduced cache misses. Modern CPUs often allow unaligned access, but performance may be slightly slower than aligned access in some cases.
